desc: The SD root's t6040-net-up runs as an inittab ::once: entry but WiFi/sshd were not confirmed up on the maxcpus=1 boot (no address reported). Verify and fix: check wpa_supplicant associates from the baked /etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf, udhcpc gets a lease, sshd starts with the 98-byte authorized_keys, and ntpd corrects the clock. Success = the machine is reachable over ssh straight after a cold boot with no console interaction, which removes the serial tether from every future userspace iteration. ACHIEVED 2026-08-03: wlan0 associated with a DHCP lease (192.168.10.157/24, SSID Bilbo Laggins) and hci0 up, on a cold unattended boot; verified BY SSH from the host together with the i3 desktop. ROOT CAUSE of the earlier missing wlan0 was NOT missing files (my first read was wrong -- a truncated ls misled me; every WLAN blob was on the card). It was ORDERING: brcmfmac probes at 0.65s but switch_root happens at ~3.5s, so the firmware request hit the tiny initramfs and fell through to the generic brcmfmac4388c0-pcie.bin (-2). RULE: firmware requested during probe must live in the INITRAMFS, not the real root -- applies to brcmfmac, hci_bcm4377 and the trackpad HIDF blob too. Fixed by staging WLAN+BT firmware into initramfs-sdroot.cpio.gz with the c2-under-c0 mapping (hash-verified 7cfae862); initramfs 1.8 -> 8.8 MB, still 11x under the image size that loses the unpack race. The serial tether is no longer needed for userspace work.
